newsitem.title: UK: Italian minister blasts European Commission report.
newsitem.headline: Italian minister blasts European Commission report.

text.p: Italian Foreign Trade Minister Augusto Fantozzi on Monday blasted the European Commission for criticising Italy's state spending controls and said Brussels had to treat all EU countries in a similar fashion.

Earlier, the Commission recommended to EU member states that they should tell Italy it was falling short of a key economic goal needed to join the planned single European currency and that its current spending controls were "insufficient".
"This is an unacceptable position," Fantozzi told reporters on a visit to the Italian trade office in Britain.
"Treasury controls on public spending are stringent and the results prove that the deficit in the first part of the year is around half of that in the same period in 1996," Fantozzi added.

The trade minister was also angered by a Commission recommendation that Italy would need a 1998 budget deficit well below the three percent target laid down in the Maastricht Treaty for single currency aspirants.
"There is no reason to demand things of us that aren't being demanded of other states," Fantozzi said, adding: "We have to respect the stability pact and we will do that."

The stabiltiy pact establishes penalties for countries which miss government spending targets. Italy had a deficit/GDP ratio of 6.7 percent in 1996 but has vowed to cut this to the three percent threshold in 1997.
